notice: These are illustrative projects inspired by common work activities, not assignments attributed to a named company. Your answers suggest things to explore; they do not measure skill or predict a career.

software.label: Software development
software.try_it: Sketch a tiny app that solves one problem in your day. Build one small part and test what happens when an input is wrong.

data.label: Data analysis
data.try_it: Use a small public dataset to ask one question, make a chart, and explain one limitation of your answer.

design.label: Product and user experience design
design.try_it: Ask two people how they complete a simple task in an app, then sketch a clearer version and explain your choices.

robotics.label: Robotics and physical systems
robotics.try_it: Draw how a sensor, a decision and a movement connect. Try a small simulation and compare two conditions.

research.label: Research and experimentation
research.try_it: Pick a testable question, write two possible explanations, and plan a small comparison that could distinguish them.

security.label: Cybersecurity and privacy
security.try_it: Map where a fictional app stores user data and who can access it. Suggest one improvement without accessing anyone else's systems.

scenarios.title: Keep a checkout working
scenarios.problem: A shopping app sometimes loses an order when a customer taps Pay twice.
scenarios.activity: As an intern, you would reproduce the problem, follow what the app does, build a fix and test it. Some of the work is patiently finding why something failed.
scenarios.question: How interested are you in building and testing that fix?

scenarios.title: Understand unsold food
scenarios.problem: A cafeteria prepares too much food on some days and runs out on others.
scenarios.activity: You would clean daily records, look for patterns, compare predictions with actual demand and explain where the data could mislead the team.
scenarios.question: How interested are you in finding patterns and checking the prediction?

scenarios.title: Make booking less confusing
scenarios.problem: People abandon a clinic's booking app because they cannot tell which appointments are available.
scenarios.activity: You would observe how people use it, listen to their difficulties, sketch clearer screens and see whether the new design helps.
scenarios.question: How interested are you in understanding users and redesigning the experience?

scenarios.title: Help a robot navigate
scenarios.problem: A small warehouse robot must deliver boxes while people move through its route.
scenarios.activity: You would connect sensor readings to movement decisions, try safe simulations and compare how the robot behaves when its surroundings change.
scenarios.question: How interested are you in making a physical system respond to its surroundings?

scenarios.title: Compare two packaging ideas
scenarios.problem: A team wants to know which of two new packages keeps fruit fresh longer.
scenarios.activity: You would design a fair comparison, control what stays the same, record observations and explain what the experiment can and cannot show.
scenarios.question: How interested are you in testing explanations through a careful experiment?

scenarios.title: Protect a shared account system
scenarios.problem: A fictional school's app lets users see more information than their role should allow.
scenarios.activity: With permission in a test environment, you would map access rules, check how mistakes happen and help the team prevent them without making the app difficult to use.
scenarios.question: How interested are you in investigating access and protecting information?

scenarios.title: Build a tool for researchers
scenarios.problem: A lab repeats a calculation by hand every time it changes one setting in an experiment.
scenarios.activity: You would write a small tool, check its outputs against known examples and improve it so other researchers can use it reliably.
scenarios.question: How interested are you in creating reliable software that helps a research team?

scenarios.title: Separate a signal from noise
scenarios.problem: A lab's measurements suggest a change, but the instruments are noisy.
scenarios.activity: You would organise observations, plot comparisons, investigate unusual readings and explain how certain the apparent pattern is.
scenarios.question: How interested are you in analysing evidence before drawing a conclusion?

scenarios.title: Study a learning experience
scenarios.problem: A research team is testing whether a new lesson app is understandable to students using it for the first time.
scenarios.activity: You would plan observations, ask students about confusing steps, compare interface ideas and describe what improved their experience.
scenarios.question: How interested are you in studying people and improving how a product feels to use?

scenarios.title: Test a robot in dim light
scenarios.problem: A robot spots obstacles in daylight but misses them in a darker room.
scenarios.activity: You would compare sensor readings, try changes to how the robot detects obstacles and measure whether the improvement works across different conditions.
scenarios.question: How interested are you in combining experiments, software and a physical machine?

scenarios.title: Find out why seedlings grow differently
scenarios.problem: Seedlings in two parts of a lab grow at different speeds, and the reason is unclear.
scenarios.activity: You would read what is already known, propose explanations, plan controlled tests and revise your explanation when results disagree with it.
scenarios.question: How interested are you in working on a question without a known answer?

scenarios.title: Study privacy without exposing people
scenarios.problem: A lab wants to compare ways to share useful statistics while protecting individual records.
scenarios.activity: Using fictional data, you would study what each method reveals, test possible weaknesses and explain the trade-off between usefulness and privacy.
scenarios.question: How interested are you in investigating privacy and comparing protective methods?
